idea-plugin.name: Commit Message Convention Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Validates the commit message you are currently writing, live, in the IntelliJ VCS Commit dialog -- against the Conventional Commits convention -- and shows the exact rule it breaks before you commit, instead of silently accepting or rejecting.

What it checks (v0.1, Conventional Commits standard, all Free):

  • First line matches <type>(<scope>): <description> or <type>: <description> (scope is optional).
  • <type> is one of the standard, case-sensitive types: feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, perf, test, build, ci, chore, revert.
  • Subject line length: a hard warning past 72 characters (the widely-used "hard cap" for `git log --oneline` readability), a softer heads-up between 51 and 72 (above the 50-character "ideal" but still commonly accepted).
  • Description does not end with a period.

What it deliberately skips: merge commits (git-generated messages like Merge branch 'x' into 'y' are never written by hand and are never validated).

What v0.1 does NOT cover (honest scope, see README for the full list): commit footers (BREAKING CHANGE:, Refs:), the ! breaking-change marker after type/scope, and configurable team rules (custom scope whitelist, custom regex, team-specific length limits) -- that is a distinct, larger feature intentionally left for a future version, not silently half-implemented here.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no popups.
